guide.title: Operations guide
guide.subtitle: How to convert a store to an independent store, and who controls each payment method.
guide.convertIntro: A store starts as a marketplace store: the creator resells provider products, the platform collects the payment and splits it between the provider, the creator and the platform commission. An independent store sells only the creator's own products and collects payments directly on the creator's own Stripe or Kustom account, with no platform commission.
guide.marketplaceDesc: Provider catalog + own products. Payments on the platform account, payouts by transfers, commission applies.
guide.independentDesc: Own products only. Payments go straight to the creator's Stripe (Standard) or Kustom account. No commission.
guide.before1: The store's catalog should already be the creator's own products. Provider products and custom products (designs on provider products) are hidden from the storefront the moment the type changes.
guide.before2: Paid orders are never touched. Unpaid orders (awaiting card payment, or cash on delivery) are recalculated: the creator receives the full order total and no commission is recorded.
guide.before3: The store currency is reset to the platform default. The creator picks a new currency afterwards if they need one.
guide.before4: Card payments stop until the creator reconnects Stripe: an independent store needs a Standard account, which cannot be created by converting the existing Express account.
guide.convertStep1Body: Go to Creators, open the creator, and in the Store card choose Store type: Independent, then press Save. There is no confirmation dialog; the change is applied immediately.
guide.convertStep2Body: The storefront cache is refreshed, provider and custom products disappear from the store, the currency is cleared to the platform default and unpaid orders are recalculated with 100% of the total for the creator.
guide.convertStep3Body: In the creator dashboard, Settings, the Stripe card shows Reconnect required. Clicking Reconnect Stripe creates a new Standard account and opens Stripe onboarding (identity and bank details). Card payments are enabled only when Stripe reports charges enabled.
guide.convertStep4Body: In Settings, the Store currency selector appears for independent stores only. Leaving it empty keeps the platform default. Kustom is only offered for currencies it processes (SEK, NOK, DKK, EUR, GBP, USD and a few more).
guide.convertStep5Body: Still in Settings: turn on Cash on delivery if wanted, and set up Kustom Checkout with the creator's own Merchant ID and shared secret, test the connection, switch the environment to Production and enable it.
guide.convertStep6Body: Back on the creator page the type shows Independent. In platform Settings make sure the Stripe Connect webhook secret is configured: without it, refunds the creator makes in their own Stripe dashboard never reach the platform. Place a small test order to confirm checkout works.
guide.effect1: Rejects provider and custom items at checkout and hides them from the storefront.
guide.effect2: Writes commission records with platform 0, provider 0, creator = order total.
guide.effect3: Charges card payments directly on the creator's Standard account (no transfers).
guide.effect4: Offers Kustom Checkout at checkout only when the creator has enabled it with valid credentials.
guide.revertBody: Choose Marketplace again on the creator page. The currency is cleared, unpaid orders are recalculated with the commission model, and the creator must reconnect Stripe once more (an Express payout account is created). Kustom is hidden automatically because it is only offered to independent stores.
guide.paymentsIntro: Payment methods are switched on and off per store by the creator from their Settings page. The admin owns the platform-level configuration (Stripe keys, webhook secrets, Kustom partner id) and the store type, which decides which methods a store may use at all.
guide.methodCodWhere: Creator dashboard, Settings, Cash on delivery
guide.methodCodConditions: Off by default. Any store type.
guide.methodStripeBy: Admin: platform keys. Creator: connect / disconnect the account
guide.methodStripeWhere: Admin Settings, Payments; Creator Settings, Stripe card
guide.methodStripeConditions: Marketplace: Express account with payouts enabled. Independent: Standard account with charges enabled. Disconnecting stops card payments immediately.
guide.methodKustomBy: Creator (credentials + enable toggle). Admin: optional partner id
guide.methodKustomWhere: Creator Settings, Kustom Checkout card; Admin Settings, Payments
guide.methodKustomConditions: Independent stores only, active store, supported currency, Merchant ID and shared secret saved, toggle enabled. Environment must be Production for real payments.
guide.adminNoteTitle: What the admin can and cannot do
guide.adminNote1: There is no per-store on/off switch for payment methods on the admin side; ask the creator to change it in their Settings, or change the store type to remove Kustom altogether.
guide.adminNote2: Clearing the Stripe keys in platform Settings disables card payments for every store at once, including independent stores.
guide.adminNote3: The Kustom partner id in platform Settings only identifies the platform to Kustom; it does not enable or disable Kustom for any store.
guide.kustomStepsTitle: Enabling Kustom Checkout for a store
guide.kustomStep1Body: In Settings, Kustom Checkout: paste the Merchant ID and shared secret from the Kustom merchant portal (the same ones used by an existing shop, for example a WordPress site, work here too).
guide.kustomStep2Body: Save, then press Test connection. Use Playground for a trial run and switch to Production before taking real payments.
guide.kustomStep3Body: Turn the Enabled toggle on and save. The option appears at checkout immediately for customers of that store.
guide.kustomStep4Body: Kustom orders are authorized at checkout and captured automatically when the order is marked as shipped. Capture and refund can also be done from the order page in the dashboard.
